claims.claim: Independent peer-market evidence supports the existing CF contradiction that stronger nitrogen pricing can coexist with weaker physical volumes. Reuters reported on 2026-07-17 that Yara's Q2 EBITDA excluding special items rose 39% year over year to $906M while deliveries fell 17%; higher margins added $520M to EBITDA while lower volumes/mix reduced EBITDA by $240M, with management saying elevated prices caused farmers to defer purchases.

A second independent peer observation points the same direction: Reuters reported on 2026-08-06 that Nutrien's Q2 nitrogen sales volumes fell 25.3% while firm nitrogen pricing supported revenue, and Nutrien expected global nitrogen markets to remain tight in H2 2026 because of trade disruptions, production outages, elevated energy prices and strong import demand from India and Brazil.

risks.risk: Industry-wide price/volume divergence means CF's strong pricing cannot by itself establish broad end-demand strength; delayed farmer purchases, outages and trade/energy disruptions can temporarily support price while suppressing volumes.

contradictions.contradiction: CF's strong earnings/pricing alongside lower volumes is directionally consistent with independently observed 2026 nitrogen-market behavior at Yara and Nutrien, reducing the likelihood that the divergence is unique to CF while not resolving CF-specific normalization or outage effects.

unknowns.unknown: Peer evidence does not establish CF-specific normalized earnings, Yazoo City restart execution, future nitrogen prices, or whether delayed demand converts into later CF volumes.

assist.outcome: added two materially independent peer-market sources supporting price-volume normalization context without creating numeric underwriting
